full_text_checked: Full text of arXiv PDFs of IoU-Net (all sections, Tables 1-4, Fig. 2-3, 7), ATOM (main paper Sec. 3-4, Tables 1-5, supplementary S5-S6 text), GFL (main paper Sec. 3-4, Tables 1-4; supplementary partly skimmed) and SiamFC++ (Sec. 3 quality branch, Table 1, Appendix C Table 4) was extracted with PyMuPDF and read. Code repositories were not opened or run; the figure scatter plots were read only via captions. Supplementary materials of GFL (IoU vs centerness details) and ATOM per-attribute plots were not examined in detail.
task_and_output: IoU-Net: two-stage COCO object detection; an extra head predicts, for each candidate box, its IoU with the matched ground truth (a scalar 'localization confidence'), used (a) as the ranking key in IoU-guided NMS instead of classification confidence and (b) as an objective for gradient-ascent box refinement. ATOM: generic single-object tracking (box output); an offline-trained, target-conditioned IoU predictor IoU(B) = g(c(x0,B0) * z(x,B)) estimates the overlap of a candidate box B in the test frame with the target defined by the reference box B0; boxes are refined by maximizing predicted IoU; a separate online classifier gives coarse position and target confidence. GFL: dense one-stage COCO detection; the classification output at the true class is trained to equal the IoU of the predicted box (joint classification-IoU score, QFL) and box sides are predicted as discrete distributions (DFL). SiamFC++: Siamese single-object tracking; a 1x1 conv quality branch predicts PSS (centerness-like score) or IoU; final box selected by classification score multiplied by quality.
data_and_independent_videos: IoU-Net: COCO trainval35k (~115k images) for training, minival (5k images) for evaluation; images, no videos. ATOM: IoU predictor trained offline on training splits of LaSOT and TrackingNet plus synthetic pairs from COCO (image pairs within a video at most 50 frames apart); evaluation on NFS (100 videos, 30 FPS version), UAV123 (123 videos), combined NFS+UAV123 = 223 videos for analysis/ablation, TrackingNet test (511 videos), LaSOT test (280 videos), VOT2018 (60 videos). Test videos are disjoint from training videos (benchmark splits), but hyper-parameters and ablations were chosen on the same NFS+UAV123 set that is also reported as a result. Supplementary S5: ATOM-VID trained on ImageNet-VID only. GFL: COCO trainval35k train, minival ablation, test-dev (20k) final. SiamFC++: training on VID, Youtube-BB, COCO, DET, LaSOT, GOT-10k (varies by line); quality-head ablation on GOT-10k val (videos disjoint from GOT-10k train) [uncertain: whether the GOT-10k val videos were also used for model selection is not stated].
target_size_and_input_resolution: IoU-Net: images resized to 800 px short side, max 1200 px long side; COCO objects of all sizes (APS/APM/APL not separately analysed for quality). ATOM: features from 288x288 patches covering 5 times the estimated target size (target occupies roughly 288/5 ~ 58 px per side in the patch, derived, not stated); offline training patches of about 5^2 times the target area. GFL: standard mmdetection COCO resolution (1333x800 style, details in supplementary) [uncertain]. SiamFC++: search image 303x303 for the head ablation (Appendix C). None operate on a 721-hexal grey lattice or on targets of ~9x12 lattice steps.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: IoU-Net and GFL: still images, no temporal dimension. ATOM: native video frame rates of benchmarks (NFS 30 FPS version, UAV123 drone footage with strong camera motion, TrackingNet/LaSOT YouTube videos with handheld/moving cameras); tracker runs >30 FPS on a GTX-1080. SiamFC++: generic tracking benchmarks with camera motion; frame rate of benchmarks, not studied as a factor.
detector_and_exemplar: IoU-Net: inside a detector (FPN/Mask R-CNN/Cascade R-CNN); candidates are detector boxes. ATOM: no detector; exemplar is the first-frame annotated box B0, encoded once into a modulation vector c(x0,B0); online classifier is updated from the tracker's own estimated states (Gaussian label at estimated position). SiamFC++: exemplar is the first-frame template crop; no detector. GFL: is itself a detector.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: IoU-Net: two-layer FC IoU head (1024-d, class-aware) on PrRoI-pooled FPN features; smooth-L1 loss on IoU normalized to [-1,1]; trained on jittered ground-truth boxes, keeping only IoU >= 0.5 and sampling uniformly over IoU; can be standalone or jointly trained with FPN (160k iterations, batch 16). ATOM: IoU predictor head (reference branch + test branch, modulation by channel-wise vector, PrPool on ResNet-18 block3+block4) trained with MSE on normalized IoU; 16 candidate boxes per image pair from Gaussian noise on ground truth with minimum IoU 0.1; backbone frozen; 40 epochs, 64 pairs per batch, Adam lr 1e-3. Online classifier: 2-layer conv (1x1 to 64 channels, then 4x4 to 1 channel), L2 loss on Gaussian labels, Gauss-Newton + conjugate gradient. Parameter counts not given. GFL: QFL(sigma) = -|y - sigma|^beta * [(1-y)log(1-sigma) + y log(sigma)], y = IoU of predicted box for positives and 0 for all negatives, beta = 2; DFL cross-entropy on two neighbouring bins of the box-side distribution. SiamFC++: focal loss for classification, BCE for quality (PSS or IoU, positives only), IoU loss for regression.
controls_seeds_splits: IoU-Net: matched comparisons of the same detector with standard NMS vs Soft-NMS vs IoU-guided NMS (Table 1), with vs without refinement (Table 2), joint training vs baseline (Table 3); single run per configuration, no seeds or confidence intervals. ATOM: each tracking result averaged over 5 runs (stochastic proposals), no CI; matched ablations: no reference branch (baseline), concatenation vs Siamese vs modulation, block3 vs block4 (Table 1); IoU-based estimation vs brute-force multi-scale search with classifier confidence (Table 2, 'Multi-Scale'), no classifier, GD vs Gauss-Newton, no hard negative mining. GFL: matched variants on two detectors (FCOS, ATSS): no quality branch, centerness branch, IoU branch, centerness-guided, IoU-guided, joint QFL (Table 1a); beta sweep (Table 1c); QFL/DFL factorial (Table 3); single runs, no seeds. SiamFC++: GOT-10k val, quality = None / PSS / IoU with otherwise identical GoogLeNet model (Table 4, lines 6-8); single runs. No source uses video-level bootstrap or reports variance of the quality-head effect.
metrics_and_numbers: IoU-Net Fig. 2 (caption): for detected boxes with IoU > 0.5 against ground truth (FPN, COCO minival), Pearson correlation of IoU with classification confidence = 0.217, with predicted IoU (localization confidence) = 0.617.

IoU-Net Sec. 2.1 / Fig. 3: with traditional NMS more than half of detected boxes with IoU > 0.9 are suppressed. Sec. 4.1: recall at matching IoU 0.9 is 18.7% after traditional NMS, 28.9% after IoU-guided NMS, 39.7% No-NMS upper bound (ResNet50-FPN).

IoU-Net Table 1 (COCO minival, standalone IoU-Net): FPN AP 36.4 / AP50 58.0 / AP90 9.8; +Soft-NMS 36.8 / 57.5 / 10.3; +IoU-NMS 37.3 / 56.0 / 13.3. Cascade R-CNN 40.6 / 59.3 / 16.7; +Soft-NMS 40.9 / 58.2 / 17.8; +IoU-NMS 40.7 / 58.0 / 18.9. Mask R-CNN 37.5 / 58.6 / 10.9; +Soft-NMS 37.9; +IoU-NMS 38.1 / 56.4 / 14.6. Note: ranking by predicted IoU lowers AP50 in every row while raising AP80-AP90.
IoU-Net Table 2 (optimization refinement): FPN 36.4 -> 38.0 AP (AP90 9.8 -> 14.6); Cascade R-CNN 40.6 -> 41.4 (AP90 16.7 -> 19.5); Mask R-CNN 37.5 -> 39.2 (AP90 10.9 -> 16.4).

IoU-Net Table 3 (joint training): ResNet-50 FPN 36.4 -> IoU-Net 37.0 -> +IoU-NMS 37.6 -> +Refine 38.1; ResNet-101 FPN 38.5 -> 38.9 -> 40.0 -> 40.6. Sec. 4.3 attributes the lower AP50 to IoU estimation error for low-IoU boxes (Fig. 2b) and says sampling more low-IoU boxes in training partially fixes it. Table 4: inference 0.305 s/image vs 0.255 s for FPN.

ATOM Table 1 (NFS+UAV123, 223 videos, mean of 5 runs, AUC %): no reference branch 56.7; modulation block3&4 62.3; concatenation 56.3; Siamese 61.7; modulation block3 only 60.3; block4 only 58.5. OP0.75: 38.6 / 48.4 / 37.9 / 47.6 / 44.5 / 38.9.

ATOM Table 2 (same set): full ATOM AUC 62.3, OP0.50 76.3, OP0.75 48.4; Multi-Scale (classifier confidence over 5 scales, ratio 1.02, no IoU predictor) AUC 53.7, OP0.50 66.2, OP0.75 26.0; No Classif 43.0; GD 60.9; GD++ 61.1; No HN 61.9. This is the closest 'confidence ranking vs IoU-quality ranking' ablation: selecting scale by classifier confidence loses 8.6 AUC points and roughly halves OP0.75.

ATOM state of the art (Sec. 4.3): NFS AUC 59.0 (Fig. 4a), UAV123 AUC 65.0 (Fig. 4b), TrackingNet success 70.3 / precision 64.8 / norm. precision 77.1 (Table 3), LaSOT success 51.5 / norm. precision 57.6 (Table 4), VOT2018 EAO 0.401, accuracy 0.590, robustness 0.204 (Table 5). Supplementary S5: ATOM-VID (ImageNet-VID only) is 2.0 AUC lower on LaSOT and 0.5 lower on TrackingNet than ATOM.

ATOM Sec. 3.3: inference uses 10 jittered proposals, 5 gradient-ascent steps on predicted IoU with step length 1, final box = mean of the 3 boxes with highest predicted IoU; target declared lost when classifier score < 0.25 (classifier confidence, not IoU, controls absence).

GFL Table 1a (COCO minival, ResNet-50, 1x; FCOS / ATSS AP): w/o quality branch 37.8 / 38.0; centerness branch 38.5 / 39.2; IoU branch 38.7 / 39.6; centerness-guided 37.9 / 38.2; IoU-guided 38.2 / 38.9; joint w/ QFL 39.0 / 39.9. Table 1b: QFL adds 0.6-0.8 AP to RetinaNet (35.6 -> 36.4), FoveaBox (36.4 -> 37.0), SSD512 (29.4 -> 30.2). Table 1c: beta 0 / 1 / 2 / 2.5 / 4 -> AP 37.6 / 39.0 / 39.9 / 39.7 / 38.2. Table 3 (ATSS): baseline 39.2, +QFL 39.9, +DFL 39.5, both 40.2, FPS unchanged 19.4. Abstract/Table 4: 45.0 AP on COCO test-dev with ResNet-101.

GFL Fig. 2 (qualitative): with a separately trained IoU branch, background patches receive predicted IoU > 0.9 (example cls 0.095 / IoU 0.927 and cls 0.101 / IoU 0.913); scatter shows weak correlation between separately predicted class and IoU scores. Cause stated in Sec. 1: quality supervised on positives only, so negatives can get uncontrolled high quality.

SiamFC++ Appendix C Table 4 (GOT-10k val, GoogLeNet, 2xconv3x3 head, single run): quality = None SR0.5 88.6 / AO 77.1; PSS 88.8 / 77.8; IoU 89.3 / 78.0. Sec. 'Quality Assessment Choice' repeats AO 77.8 (PSS) vs 78.0 (IoU). Table 1 (VOT2018) adds regression and PSS together (EAO 0.306 -> 0.400), so it does not isolate the quality head.
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: IoU-Net/GFL not applicable (images; test images unseen); ATOM yes (benchmark test sets disjoint from training videos); SiamFC++ yes (GOT-10k val). Target absence: IoU-Net/GFL not applicable; ATOM partially (threshold 0.25 on classifier score declares target lost; no evaluation of absence detection reported); SiamFC++ not reported. Similar distractors: ATOM yes qualitatively (hard negative mining for distractor peaks, +0.4 AUC; UAV123 'similar objects' attribute plot in S6), not for the IoU head itself; others not reported. Occlusion: ATOM via UAV123 attributes (full/partial occlusion plots in S6, no numbers extracted); GFL mentions occlusion only for DFL qualitative examples; IoU-Net not reported. Night or low light: not reported in any (UAV123 'illumination variation' attribute only in ATOM S6). Sequential operation on own predictions: ATOM yes (classifier trained online on its own estimated boxes; IoU predictor conditioned on first frame only); SiamFC++ yes (tracking); IoU-Net/GFL no.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: (1) Train a separate head to regress the actual quality (IoU with ground truth) of a candidate output, using candidates generated by perturbing the ground truth so that the full range of quality is covered (IoU-Net: uniform over IoU 0.5-1; ATOM: Gaussian jitter, IoU >= 0.1, 16 per pair). (2) Use predicted quality, not classification confidence, to rank or choose among candidates (IoU-NMS; ATOM top-3 by predicted IoU; SiamFC++ cls x quality), and optionally optimize the candidate by gradient ascent on predicted quality. (3) GFL adds that quality must be supervised also on negatives (target 0) and fused into the same score used at test time; otherwise the separately trained quality is unreliable exactly where it matters (background gets high quality). Evidence: classification confidence correlates weakly with localization quality (Pearson 0.217 vs 0.617 for predicted IoU, IoU-Net Fig. 2); quality ranking mostly helps the high-precision regime (AP80-AP90) and can hurt the loose regime (AP50 drops 1-2 points in IoU-Net Table 1); in tracking, IoU-based estimation beats classifier-confidence multi-scale search by 8.6 AUC (ATOM Table 2), while a quality head on top of classification in SiamFC++ gives only +0.7-0.9 AO. Proposed modification (ours, not published): define the FlyVis readout's intervention score as a predicted 'usefulness quality' q = P(error of corrected centre < error of standard ByteTrack/Kalman prediction) or a regression of the error reduction, trained on all candidate situations (including negatives where no correction is useful, target 0), and use q both to rank and to gate the correction.
transfer_limits: 1) Target definition: published targets are IoU of a box with ground truth, a quantity defined for every candidate; our usefulness target is relative (corrected-centre error minus standard-prediction error), depends on the Kalman prediction quality, and is undefined or noisy when ground truth is missing or ambiguous (BDD100K MOT ID switches, occlusions). 2) Candidate generation: IoU-Net/ATOM train on synthetic jitter around ground truth; our candidates come from FlyVis readout on real moving and rescaling crops (square max(2 x long side, 64 px)) at 30 Hz with 721 grey hexals, so synthetic jitter would mismatch the real error distribution; ATOM itself needed large tracking datasets (LaSOT+TrackingNet+COCO) and the IoU head has no distractor discrimination (No Classif AUC 43.0). 3) Our hard case is choosing the previous target among similar neighbours or refusing; IoU heads measure geometric overlap given the right object and are blind to identity (ATOM leaves absence and distractors to the online classifier). A usefulness head must therefore combine identity and localization, which is GFL's joint representation, not IoU-Net's separate one. 4) Scale: targets ~9.37 x 12.06 lattice steps on a coarse hexagonal grid; IoU on such grids is quantized, so a centre-error target in lattice steps or pixels is more suitable than IoU. 5) Class imbalance and tail: we need the top 1% of scores to be reliable (currently 7 of 37 known useful); published works report average ranking metrics (AP, AUC), not precision in the extreme top tail, and IoU-Net notes poorer quality estimates for low-IoU boxes. 6) Sample size: our training data are ~104 train videos (train104/train26/dev35/heldout75 split mentioned in project context); published heads are trained on 10^5 images or thousands of videos. 7) Environment: YOLO26s + XYWHByteTrack + MASA already provide detector confidence and appearance; any gain of a quality head must be shown over a no-FlyVis head (variant B) on the same features, otherwise it is a readout improvement, not a FlyVis result. 8) No source measures gains with video-level bootstrap; all effects are single-run point estimates (ATOM: 5-run means).
research_questions_addressed: Q4 (primary, direct design evidence): shows that a separately trained quality head ranks candidates better than classification confidence (IoU-Net Fig. 2, Tables 1-3; ATOM Table 2; SiamFC++ Table 4) and that quality must be supervised on negatives and fused with the decision score to avoid spuriously high quality on wrong candidates (GFL Fig. 2, Table 1a) - this matches our symptom that high presence probability does not mean a useful correction. Caution for Q4: effects are on in-distribution benchmarks, no evaluation under distribution shift or extreme-tail precision. Q2 (design analogy): ATOM Table 1 shows that what is fed to the quality head (reference-conditioned modulation, block3+4 features) changes AUC by up to 6 points with fixed training, i.e. readout architecture can dominate; a separate quality head allows testing whether FlyVis features carry usefulness information beyond the no-FlyVis features. Q5 (practical): a small quality head (two FC layers) is cheap and fits 12 GB; the control without FlyVis is straightforward. Q1 and Q3: not informed (no exemplar-among-distractors or eye-resolution evidence; ATOM delegates distractors to the online classifier).
candidate_node_change: Node: readout (FlyVis output-cell activity -> intervention decision). Change: add a usefulness-quality output to the FlyVis readout, trained jointly with the centre output with a GFL-style quality focal loss. Target per (track, frame) during loss: y = 1 if ||corrected centre - GT centre|| < ||standard prediction - GT centre|| by a margin (e.g. >= 1 lattice step or relative 20%), soft version y = clip(error reduction / standard error, 0, 1); y = 0 for all situations where the correction is not useful, including target absent, wrong neighbour chosen and no GT match (supervised negatives, the key GFL point). Candidate augmentation as in IoU-Net/ATOM: in addition to the readout's own argmax, score K jittered/neighbour candidate centres per crop (including the centres of similar neighbouring detections) with their true usefulness, sampled uniformly over error reduction. Intervention rule: apply the correction only when q > tau, tau chosen on dev35 for a fixed coverage (e.g. top 1-5%) and then frozen. Controls, identical data and splits: (B) same quality head on the no-FlyVis network (~9602 params) features; (C) stock frozen FlyVis + same head; (D) trained FlyVis + same head; plus (B0) ranking by current presence probability (the existing score) and (DET) ranking by YOLO detection confidence of the matched neighbour. Minimal check (cheap, no HOTA first): on dev35 and heldout75 with video-level splits, compute precision of useful corrections in the top 1% / 5% of q vs presence probability, Spearman correlation of q with true error reduction, with paired video-level bootstrap CI; require q(D or C) > q(B) in precision@1% with CI excluding 0 and better than presence probability (currently 7 of 37 known useful in top 1%). Only then one HOTA run on heldout75 with stand / stand+B / stand+D. Stop condition: if precision@top1% of q on heldout75 does not exceed presence probability by a pre-registered margin (e.g. +10 percentage points) or if q(D) - q(B) CI includes 0, stop this action and record the readout as the failing node; replacement options are an online target model per track (DiMP-style, item I8) or conformal gating (item I10).
strongest_objection: The published gains come from ranking geometric overlap of candidates that already belong to the right object, with large in-distribution training sets; our failure is identity (re-finding the previous target among similar neighbours or refusing) under scarce, video-correlated labels. A usefulness head trained on ~100 videos may simply learn the base rate and tracker-state cues (track age, Kalman covariance, detection density) that are available without FlyVis, so any improvement is likely attributable to the readout and environment, not to FlyVis (variant B may match D). Moreover, the direct tracking evidence for a separate quality head beyond confidence is small (SiamFC++: +0.7-0.9 AO, single run), and IoU-Net shows quality ranking can hurt the loose-threshold regime (AP50 -1.5 to -2.2), which is analogous to HOTA's association component where choosing the right identity matters more than precise centring.
evidence_strength: IoU-Net (ECCV), ATOM (CVPR), GFL (NeurIPS), SiamFC++ (AAAI) are peer-reviewed and widely replicated in follow-ups (PrDiMP, DiMP family, GFLV2, VarifocalNet, mmdetection integration); code is public for ATOM (pytracking), GFL (GFocal, mmdetection), SiamFC++ (video_analyst), only PrRoIPooling for IoU-Net; code not run here. Overall: strong for the general claim that a learned quality head ranks localization better than classification confidence on in-distribution benchmarks; weak for our specific claim (usefulness of a correction relative to a baseline prediction, identity among similar neighbours, extreme-tail precision, distribution shift), because no source tests it and all ablations are single-run without confidence intervals.
